text: Adult dogs generally need 20-60 minutes of walking or active play per day, split across 1-3 sessions, to stay physically and mentally healthy.
Most adult dogs do well on two measured meals a day, roughly 10-15 minutes each including cleanup, at consistent times to support digestion.
Brushing a dog 2-3 times a week for about 10 minutes reduces shedding and matting; nail trims are typically needed every 2-4 weeks.
Short training or puzzle-toy sessions of 10-15 minutes a day give dogs mental stimulation that tires them out as much as physical exercise.
Litter boxes should be scooped once a day, a 5-10 minute task, to prevent odor buildup and litter-box avoidance.
Cats typically do best with 2-4 small measured meals a day, each taking about 5-10 minutes to prepare and serve.
Interactive play with a wand toy for 10-20 minutes a day satisfies a cat's hunting instinct and reduces destructive behavior.
Weekly brushing sessions of about 10 minutes help control shedding and hairballs, especially for long-haired cats.
For small mammals, birds, and reptiles, a brief 5-10 minute daily check of food, water, and habitat conditions catches problems early.
Rotating toys or habitat enrichment items every few days for about 10 minutes keeps small pets and exotics from becoming bored or stressed.
Medication or supplement administration should happen at the same time daily, usually 5 minutes, so owners can track missed doses easily.
Routine wellness checks are recommended roughly every 6-12 months; a reminder task the week before an appointment reduces no-shows.
